record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: For which strong-amalgamation-property Fraisse classes K does the Fraisse limit of K have finite big Ramsey degrees? Here the strong amalgamation property means that when two finite structures are amalgamated over a common finite substructure, the two embedded copies intersect exactly in the embedded common part. In particular, decide whether finite big Ramsey degrees always exist for SAP Fraisse classes with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, whether they always exist for such classes when all relation arities are at most two, and find a general condition characterizing the SAP classes whose Fraisse limits have finite big Ramsey degrees.

evidence.quote: A Fraı̈ssé class K satisfies the strong amalgamation property (SAP) if given A, B, C ∈ K and embeddings e : A → B and f : A → C, there is some D ∈ K and embeddings e′ : B → D and f ′ : C → D such that e′ ◦ e = f ′ ◦ f , and e′ [B] ∩ f ′ [C] = e′ ◦ e[A] = f ′ ◦ f [A].
Problem 6.1. For which SAP Fraı̈ssé classes does the Fraı̈ssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?
Subquestions are the following: Given an SAP Fraı̈ssé class with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, does its Fraı̈ssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a Fraïssé class K is a class of finite structures (in a fixed first-order signature) that is hereditary, contains only countably many isomorphism types, and satisfies the joint embedding and amalgamation properties; its Fraïssé limit is the unique up to isomorphism countable, locally finite, ultrahomogeneous structure whose age equals K. Say that K satisfies the strong amalgamation property (SAP) if for all A, B, C in K and all embeddings e: A → B and f: A → C, there exist D in K and embeddings e': B → D, f': C → D such that e' ∘ e = f' ∘ f and moreover e'[B] ∩ f'[C] = e' ∘ e[A].

Let M be the Fraïssé limit of K, and for a finite substructure A ⊆ M let the big Ramsey degree of A in M, denoted T(A, M), be the least integer t (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring of the copies of A in M there exists a substructure M' ⊆ M isomorphic to M in which the copies of A take at most t colors. We say M has finite big Ramsey degrees if T(A, M) is finite for every finite A in the age of M.

(a) Characterize the SAP Fraïssé classes K whose Fraïssé limit has finite big Ramsey degrees.

(b) In particular, decide: if K is an SAP Fraïssé class in a finite relational language and is defined by forbidding a finite set of finite substructures, must its Fraïssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?

(c) Same question as (b), but under the additional assumption that all relation symbols have arity at most 2.
artifact.category_tag: big Ramsey degrees of Fraïssé limits
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization problem is open. Substantial partial progress exists: Balko–Chodounský–Dobrinen–Hubička–Konečný–Vena and others have established finite big Ramsey degrees for free amalgamation classes in finite binary languages with finitely many forbidden irreducible substructures, and Coulson–Dobrinen–Patel obtained simply-characterized big Ramsey structures for classes with arity ≤ 2 satisfying SDAPC (a strengthening of SAP). However, no full characterization for general SAP Fraïssé classes is known, and the subquestions about classes with finitely many forbidden substructures (in arbitrary arity, and even in the binary case beyond free amalgamation) remain open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Exact big Ramsey degrees for finitely constrained binary free amalgamation classes
status_evidence.snippet: Big Ramsey degrees of free amalgamation classes in finite binary languages defined by finitely many forbidden irreducible substructures are characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: finite big Ramsey degrees established for finitely constrained binary free amalgamation classes.

status_evidence.title: Fraïssé classes with simply characterized big Ramsey structures
status_evidence.snippet: Fraïssé structures in finite relational languages with relation symbols of arity at most two having a property strengthening the Disjoint Amalgamation Property have finite big Ramsey degrees with a simple characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress for arity ≤ 2 under SDAPC, a strengthening of SAP.
